terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Radially symmetric about +Y for every feature except the head bung. This is the decisive structural fact: the whole shell is ONE swept profile, so a component split buys nothing and costs a draw call for the life of the prop.

reasoning: Silhouette is moderately complex: eight distinct profile events (base curl, lower panel, lower hoop, mid panel, upper hoop, upper panel, top curl, head plate), but all of them lie on ONE curve.
Component count is 1 for the shell plus 1 boss. Occlusion risk is near zero because a surface of revolution ENTAILS its hidden side rather than requiring it to be inferred.
Detail density carries the fidelity here, not geometry: the rust distribution, the streaks and the worn hoop crowns are what make it read as a used drum rather than a blue cylinder.
Action readiness is minimal by explicit decision: the prop is sealed, has no moving parts and is not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Depth is deliberately spent on localFeatures and material localOverrides rather than on meso COMPONENTS. The validator counts one draw call per componentTree entry, and the resolved scene budget allows two. Splitting the hoops or chimes into their own components would satisfy a template's meso count and then cost this prop two extra CPU submissions per frame, forever, for parts that are continuous with the shell surface. The anti-shallow rule is satisfied by 6+ micro feature groups and 4 material local overrides, which is where this object's real complexity lives.

detailInventory.scanMethod: grid-3x3 zone scan plus three targeted crops
detailInventory.note: Eight built details. A ninth -- the stencilled "1952" on the plate -- is recorded in scratch/oil-drum/detail-inventory.json and deliberately NOT built, so it is absent here rather than carrying a mapsTo that would claim geometry or a material override that does not exist.

details.observation: Convex outward bead encircling the body, centre at y = 0.287 m, crown radius 0.290 m against a body radius of 0.2788 m.
Second bead, centre y = 0.584 m, same crown radius. The two hoops divide the body into three panels of 0.326 / 0.338 / 0.336 -- equal thirds to 1.2 percent.
Rolled toroidal curl closing the shell onto the head plate, radius 0.2879 m -- proud of the body by 9.1 mm. The head plate sits BELOW the crown of the curl, recessed.
Matching curl at the bottom. It is the GROUND CONTACT at y = 0; the body panel never touches the floor.

Raised annulus of bare oxidised steel on the head plate, outer diameter 64 mm, with a recessed dark centre. Measured centre at image (697, 126); resolved to radius 0.185 m from the axis at azimuth 79 degrees from front. The ONLY feature that breaks the drum's radial symmetry.
Both chime crowns carry near-continuous orange-brown oxidation; it is the heaviest rust on the object and it follows the curl rather than pooling randomly.
Vertical rust streaks running DOWNWARD from the top chime and from each hoop, widening as they fall. Gravity-directed and top-weighted; they are not symmetric about any axis.
Pale blue-grey band with a tight highlight along each hoop crown, where the paint has worn to bare metal. This is the only near-metallic response on the object.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Adjacent components must overlap by at least 0.02 world units at shared seams (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
qualityContract.$budgetNote: macroComponents is 1 and mesoComponents is 0: the drum shell is the single macro assembly and the bung is a micro part. microFeatureGroups is 6. The resolved scene budget is 2 draw calls and validate_sculpt_spec counts one per componentTree entry, so this object's complexity is carried by localFeatures and material localOverrides -- which is where it actually lives.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

correctionAccounting.note: The loop counter reads 0/10 and that is NOT because nothing needed correcting. Loop counts derive from reviewHistory entries whose action is refine-spec or refine-code; every pass here was recorded once, with action=continue, AFTER its defects were found and fixed. So the counter measures recorded correction ROUNDS, not corrections. Read the pass summaries instead -- they carry the real list.
realCorrectionsMade: blockout: rebuilt from 0.88 m to 0.81 m after the plate and the Meshy proxy independently showed the reference drum 8 percent squat; silhouette IoU 0.8435 -> 0.9165.
blockout: enamel palette reweighted 3-rust-to-2-blue -> 4-blue-to-1-rust after the drum rendered predominantly orange.
blockout: two profile stations added to soften the chime seams, then REVERTED when they cost 176 triangles and moved the gate by one vertex.
form-refinement: bung lathe was an open shell with no underside; closing it by appending a point reversed the winding and turned it inside out; re-traced in the shell direction.
form-refinement: bung flange raised 7.5 -> 10 mm and cap recess deepened 4 -> 8 mm.
form-refinement: bung material declared textureless, halving gpuBytesEstimate 44.7 -> 22.4 MB.
material-pass: runtime referencePbr texture LOADS neutralised at the thaikit boundary; they were 404ing and rendering the drum black.
material-pass: all physical wear placement moved from v-space to metres through a v-to-height table, after oxide spilled 144 mm up the lower panel.
material-pass: enamel range lifted off the de-lit dark stop, which sat below the review backdrop and produced false interior holes on three of four azimuths.
material-pass: bung albedo corrected twice -- second palette stop -> first stop -> direct measurement of the plate at the bung location (#605751).

featureReviewTargets.name: Rolling hoop pitch and proudness
featureReviewTargets.criterion: Hoop crowns at y = 0.26564 and 0.54031 +/- 0.010 m, dividing the body into three equal panels, each proud of the body by 11-12 mm. The FRACTIONAL heights (0.328 and 0.667) are what the plate and the Meshy proxy agree on; they are unchanged by the rescale, which is why rescaling does not weaken this target.

featureReviewTargets.name: Chimes proud of the body, base chime on the floor
featureReviewTargets.criterion: Both chimes reach 0.2870 m against the body s 0.2780 m, and the LOWEST point of the whole model is on the base chime at y = 0. A drum resting on its body panel is wrong in a way that shows the moment it is placed on a floor.

featureReviewTargets.name: Rust distribution and direction
featureReviewTargets.criterion: Heaviest at both chime crowns, streaking DOWNWARD from the top chime and each hoop, bare metal along the hoop crowns. Scored on DISTRIBUTION, never on per-blob correlation: the wear is procedural by decision (see projection-route.json), so matching individual blobs is neither expected nor desirable.

featureReviewTargets.name: Closed solid with a recessed head
featureReviewTargets.criterion: The shell caps at both ends and the head plate sits 9 mm BELOW the top chime crown. An open tube, or a head flush with the chime, both read as a bin.

featureReviewTargets.name: Rear 180 degrees is seeded, not mirrored
featureReviewTargets.criterion: Rear geometry is ENTAILED by the sweep, so only wear is at issue. The 180 and 270 degree turntable frames must not be reflections of 0 and 90.

featureReviewTargets.name: Bung position on the head
featureReviewTargets.criterion: 64 mm outer diameter at 0.185 m from the axis. It is the only break in radial symmetry, so it is also the only way to tell which way the drum faces.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Sealed rigid-body prop. One root pivot at base-center, no sockets, no destruction groups, one cylinder collider. This is a DECISION, recorded so its emptiness is not mistaken for an oversight.
authoringRules: A named pivot promises a part turns on that axis; a named socket promises something attaches there. Both are contract the kit has to keep.

This drum has no moving parts and nothing attaches to it, so it declares ONE pivot -- the root -- and ZERO sockets. A previous attempt declared two revolute bung caps; they were removed because a sealed drum does not unscrew.
Never name a marker for a place on the surface. A location is not a mechanism.

destructionPolicy.rationale: The asset declares an EMPTY destructionGroups list. promote-model.mjs checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so one invented group fails the build just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The second (3/4 inch) bung a real tight-head drum carries is not visible and is NOT modelled. Confidence one exists: 0.5.
The asset description promises a dented rim; the plate shows a geometrically ROUND rim. Observation overrides the description, so no dent is modelled.
The head plate is read as flat with a 2 mm dish; the plate centre is blown out by the studio key.
The stencilled 1952 on the plate is NOT reproduced -- a one-off marking the image model invented against an explicit no-text clause, not a feature of the prop class.

Real-world size follows the PLATE, not the ISO standard: 0.81 m tall for a 0.58 m diameter. A real 200 litre drum is 0.88 m, and both the plate silhouette and the Meshy proxy independently show this one drawn about 8 percent short. Building to 0.88 m would have meant scoring a dimensionally correct drum against a reference it could never match at any camera angle. The asset s scale.declared.h moves with it.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the camera-facing side of the plate
coordinateFrame.origin: base-center -- the axis at y = 0, which is the base chime s ground contact
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: metres. 0.58 x 0.81 x 0.58 m -- the plate s proportions. The asset s declared height was moved from the ISO 0.88 m to match, so the registry and the model agree.

silhouette.symmetry: radial about +Y, broken only by the head bung
silhouette.widestFeature: the two rolling hoops at 0.2900 m radius, NOT the chimes at 0.2870 m
silhouette.notes: That the hoops rather than the chimes are widest was established by de-trending the plate for perspective and confirmed independently by the Meshy proxy. A first read of the plate had it the other way round.
silhouette.proportionNote: 0.81 m tall for a 0.58 m diameter, which is the PLATE s drum, not the ISO 200 litre drum. Measured two ways: the plate silhouette (chime-centre span 773.9 px at a ~12 degree camera) gives 0.8098 m, and the Meshy proxy is 7.2 percent squat against the same declaration. A real drum is 0.88 m; that discrepancy is the image model s, and the decision was to build the prop the reference actually shows rather than score a correct drum against a wrong photo.

viewEvidence.notes: The single authoritative plate. Camera elevation measured at ~12 degrees.
Per-row radius profile with the perspective trend removed.
Meshy proxy, band by band. Corroborates hoop placement; its aspect ratio is rejected.

componentTree.name: Drum shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every feature except the bung lies on ONE profile swept 360 degrees: base curl, three body panels, two rolling hoops, top curl and head plate. Splitting them into components would cost a draw call each, for the life of the prop, to express parts that are continuous with the same sheet of steel.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: surface of revolution; one closed lathe, capped at both ends

latheProfile.heightScaleNote: Y scaled by 0.92045 (0.88 m -> 0.81 m) to the plate s own proportions. Radii are unchanged: they are independent measurements the plate and the Meshy proxy agree on.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 44 radial segments at the 0.29 m hoop radius gives 0.74 mm of chord error. On a 1024 px review render where the drum spans 590 px that is 0.75 px -- sub-pixel, so the silhouette cost is not resolvable. Chosen to the budget UP FRONT rather than decimated afterwards, which keeps the measured profile points exact instead of letting a quadric collapse move them.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. The prop is sealed and moves as one rigid body, so this is the ONLY pivot it has.

collider.notes: Declared cylinder on the asset. Radius is the CHIME radius, not the body radius: the chimes are what a physics query first touches.

destruction.notes: Not breakable, by explicit decision on the asset. The registry declares an EMPTY destructionGroups list and promotion checks built against declared as an equality, so a single invented group fails.

localFeatures.notes: Convex outward bead. Realised as profile points 6-9.
The two hoops divide the body into panels of 0.326 / 0.338 / 0.336 -- equal thirds.
GROUND CONTACT. Profile point 3 sits at y = 0; the body panel never touches the floor.
Highest point of the model. The head plate is RECESSED 9 mm below the curl crown.
Read as flat with a slight dish; low confidence and low consequence at a 12 degree camera.
Present so the shell is a CLOSED solid. Never seen.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: fine rolled-steel grain with oxidation pitting concentrated at both chimes
surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: paint worn through to bare metal along both hoop crowns
surfaceDetail.notes: Carried by the runtime canvas maps, not by geometry.

baseColor.notes: Enamel mid-tone as BUILT by the wear painter.

colorMaterialRecipe.finishStyle: satin enamel over rolled steel, oxidising from both rolled edges inward

stops.note: lower hoop crown, worn to bare metal

colorGradient.notes: Measured stop positions, not a decorative ramp: they are the chime and hoop heights from silhouette-measurements.json. The oxide is top- and bottom-weighted because a rolled edge is where the coating thins.

colorMaterialRecipe.consistencyNote: These hexes track the wear painter, not the raw de-lit extraction. They were left at the de-lit #1B4A5C after the enamel range was lifted, and diagnose_render -- which scores the render s dominant clusters AGAINST this recipe -- reported a per-part delta-E of 20.28 against its 20.0 threshold. That gate was measuring the spec disagreeing with itself, not the model disagreeing with the plate.

componentTree.name: Head bung
componentTree.topologyRationale: A raised annular flange with a recessed cap -- itself a small surface of revolution, about its own axis rather than the drum s.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: small surface of revolution: raised flange with a recessed cap

latheProfile.profileNote: Flange raised from 7.5 mm to 10 mm proud and the cap recess deepened from 4 mm to 8 mm. At the first form render the bung read as a 7 px crescent -- geometrically the right size, but too shallow to separate from the head plate. The plate crop shows a chunky raised collar around a clearly sunken cap. Same six points, so the triangle cost is unchanged.
latheProfile.closureNote: Closed AND wound in the same direction as the drum shell: axis at the base, out along the underside, up the outside, over the flange, back in to the axis. Two separate defects were found here. First the profile ended at (0.032, 0) and never returned to the axis, leaving an OPEN shell with no underside -- 23 of 102 vertices read as interior, because a ray-parity test on a surface with a hole is undefined rather than inaccurate. Closing it by appending (0.0001, 0) made it WORSE, 97 of 119: appending ran the profile top-to-bottom overall, which reverses LatheGeometry s winding and turns the part inside out. Re-tracing in the shell s direction fixes both. Neither showed up in the beauty render, because a 64 mm part rendered inside-out at 7 px still looks like a small dark ring.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 16 segments on a 32 mm radius is 0.19 mm of chord error. The part is 64 mm across on a 580 mm drum -- it spans about 65 px of a 1024 px review render, so more segments buy nothing measurable.

attachment.notes: Flange base is flush on the head plate; the cap is recessed inside it.

pivot.notes: NOT a mechanism. This bung does not unscrew: the prop is sealed by explicit decision, and a named pivot is a promise a game can turn it.

localFeatures.notes: The ONLY break in the drum s radial symmetry.

surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: bare steel throughout -- no paint ever covered it

componentTree.levelRationale: Reclassified macro -> micro. It is 64 mm on an 880 mm drum: a feature-scale part, not an assembly. It is a separate COMPONENT only because it breaks the radial symmetry the shell lathe depends on, which is a geometry constraint rather than a claim about its importance. Draw calls are counted per componentTree entry and are unaffected.

materials.name: Worn blue enamel over steel

albedo.samplingNotes: De-lit palette measured by extract_pbr_evidence.py from crop-paint at confidence 0.751. The broad vertical bright bands on each panel are specular response to the studio key, not albedo, and are deliberately not sampled.
albedo.renderedRangeNote: The painter authors the enamel over #24566A..#4A8098 with a #326C84 mid, which is BRIGHTER than the de-lit stops recorded in referencePbr. Recorded here because it is a deliberate deviation from the extraction, not drift. Authored at the de-lit stops the drum rendered at a median luma of 62 facing the harness key and 48 facing away, against a review backdrop of 58; turntable_gate then read the sub-backdrop regions as interior HOLES and failed. The plate s own body row measures median 67, p95 105, max 142, so every lifted stop stays inside the reference s measured range. Two separate effects were distinguished before changing anything: the render s p95 of 71 against the plate s 105 is MISSING SPECULAR -- the harness supplies three directional lights and no environment map, so a satin dielectric cannot produce the plate s broad highlight bands -- and that shortfall was deliberately NOT compensated by baking brightness into base colour.

colorVariation.pattern: gravity-directed rust streaking over mottled enamel
colorVariation.paletteNote: FOUR enamel stops to one oxide stop, deliberately. makeProceduralTextureSet mottles across the palette roughly evenly, so an earlier 3-rust-to-2-blue palette rendered the drum predominantly orange -- the inverse of the plate, where oxide is a minority region at the chimes and in the streaks. The palette sets the BASE enamel; the measured oxide placement is the wear painter's job, not the mottler's.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: One unwrap over the whole lathe. 1024 square over a 1.82 m circumference x 0.88 m shell is ~1.1 mm per texel, which resolves a rust streak edge and nothing finer. Generated once at runtime and shared by every instance in the level, so it is one upload for the whole kit rather than one per placed drum.

surfaceFrequencyBands.role: panel-scale tonal mottling in the enamel and the large rust blooms at the chimes
individual rust streaks falling from the top chime and each hoop

roughness.map: generated-roughness-canvas: 0.30 on the worn hoop crowns, 0.50 on intact enamel, 0.88 on oxidised regions
roughness.notes: Base 0.5 comes from the painted-metal finish recipe in analyze_texture.py. The pixel-derived roughnessBase of 0.784 is NOT used: extract_pbr_evidence itself warned "low value range weakens height/roughness inference" on this crop, and a 0.78 base contradicts the visible satin sheen.

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darkens the two hoop roots and both chime recesses, where a rolled edge traps dirt. Independent of albedo.

localOverrides.region: both chime curls, y < 0.03 and y > 0.855
localOverrides.notes: The heaviest oxidation on the object, near-continuous around both curls. It follows the curl rather than pooling randomly, because a rolled edge is where the coating thins.

localOverrides.region: body panels, falling from the top chime and each hoop
localOverrides.direction: downward, widening with distance from the source
localOverrides.evidenceRef: plate zones r1c1, r1c2, r2c1, r2c2
localOverrides.notes: Gravity-directed and top-weighted. Seeded independently around the full 360 degrees rather than mirrored -- mirrored wear reads as bilateral symmetry the moment the prop is orbited, which is the defect a turntable gate exists to catch.

localOverrides.region: both hoop crowns, y = 0.2886 and y = 0.5870
localOverrides.notes: Paint worn through to bare metal on the proudest band. The only near-metallic response on the object, and what gives each hoop its tight highlight.
Low-frequency tonal mottling in the enamel itself, separate from the rust. Without it the panels read as flat vinyl.

shaderNotes: Albedo, roughness, normal and AO all arrive as ONE generated canvas set at runtime; the factory ships no texture files.

metalness stays a scalar 0.0 because enamel is a dielectric coat. The rust and bare-steel regions raise their apparent metallic response through roughness and albedo alone, which is a deliberate approximation: a metalnessMap would be a fourth 1024 canvas for a difference that is not resolvable at prop scale.

analyze_texture.py proposes clearcoat 1.0 (MeshPhysicalMaterial). Shipped as MeshStandardMaterial instead: a clearcoat lobe is an extra BRDF evaluation per fragment on a prop a level builder places hundreds of, and at 0.58 m across the difference is a slightly tighter highlight. Recorded as a deliberate downgrade, not an oversight.
materials.notes: ONE material for three visual regions. A colour difference is not a material difference: enamel, rust and bare steel differ in albedo and roughness, which maps express, and giving each its own material would cost a shader switch per region.

referencePbr.notes: Confidence 0.751, above the 0.7 stop signal. The extractor warned that object/background separation is weak on this crop; that affects its height and roughness inference, which is why the roughness base is taken from the finish recipe instead.

materials.name: Bare oxidised steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured DIRECTLY off the plate at the bung s own location (x 668-726, y 110-144): mean #605751, median luma 73. That settles a disagreement between two weaker readings. It was first authored #9C8271 -- the SECOND stop of extract_pbr_evidence s palette, taken as dominant by mistake, luma 134, which rendered the bung as a pale tan disc. Correcting to the first stop #513F31 (luma 66) was the right direction; the direct measurement then places the true value just above it. extract_pbr_evidence s bung report (confidence 0.86) remains the evidence for the metalness and roughness scalars.

roughness.map: generated-roughness-canvas: oxidation mottling around a 0.70 base
roughness.notes: Taken directly from the pixel-derived roughnessBase of 0.698. Trusted here, unlike on the enamel, because this crop has a valueRange of 0.81 and drew no low-contrast warning.

ambientOcclusion.notes: The cap is recessed inside the flange; that step is the only occlusion the part has.

shaderNotes: Solid albedo, no generated maps, by an explicit textureless declaration.
A second MATERIAL rather than a region of the first because its metalness is 0.35 against the enamel s 0.0, and a scalar metalness cannot differ within one material without a metalnessMap.
materials.notes: The second and last material. maxMaterials is 2. Declared textureless -- see textureless.evidence for the measurement and the VRAM this saves.

evidence: The part is a 64 mm bung flange on a 580 mm drum. At the review framing it spans about 65 px of a 1024 px render, and in a level it is a handful of pixels -- below the scale at which any of its oxidation mottling is resolvable.

extract_pbr_evidence.py on scratch/oil-drum/crops/mat-bung.png returned confidence 0.86 with a valueRange of 0.8079, and that evidence is kept in scratch/oil-drum/pbr-bung-report.json. It is used to set the SOLID albedo #9C8271, metalness 0.35 and roughness 0.70 -- scalars, not maps.

Measured cost of not declaring this: render-model.mjs reported 8 textures and 44.7 MB of gpuBytesEstimate, against 4 textures and 22.4 MB with the shell alone. The generator was building a second full 1024 square canvas set -- albedo, roughness, normal, AO -- for a part that shows no texture. That is 22 MB of VRAM per level, for nothing a viewer can see.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: shell only, by design -- the bung is a micro component and PASS_LEVELS admits micro from form-refinement. 1672 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry against a 2000/2/2/2 ceiling. The pass's decisive event was a proportion correction: the plate draws the drum 8 percent squatter than a real ISO 200 litre drum (0.810 m for a 0.58 m diameter), corroborated independently by the Meshy proxy at 7.2 percent. Rebuilt to 0.81 m with the user's agreement and the asset's declared height moved with it; silhouette IoU rose 0.8435 to 0.9165 and aspect delta fell 0.0657 to 0.0027. self_intersection.py fails on 6 of 990 vertices; a controlled experiment (gate-evidence/) shows a minimal cylinder with one recessed end plate trips the same gate while a plain capped cylinder does not, so the geometry is kept and the false positive recorded.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural-pass: geometry identical to blockout, and that is the correct outcome rather than a skipped pass. This prop declares ONE macro component and no meso components, so the pass that exists to build the meso hierarchy has nothing to add; the bung is micro and enters at form-refinement. The parent-child relation, the single root pivot and the cylinder collider are all present and were re-checked: attachment_anchor passes with 0 attachments (the bung embeds rather than socketing), turntable covers all four azimuths without collapse or interior holes, and Tier 1 holds at IoU 0.9165 / aspect 0.0027 / scale 0.0127. self_intersection reports the same two rings as blockout -- the documented recessed-plate false positive, not a new defect.

reviewHistory.summary: Form-refinement: the bung enters (micro level) and the prop reaches 1864 triangles, 2 draw calls, 2 materials, 2 unique geometries -- at ceiling on three of the four axes and 93 percent of the triangle budget. The pass's real work was two defects self_intersection.py found in the bung that NO render showed: the lathe profile never returned to the axis, so the part was an open shell with no underside (23 of 102 vertices interior); closing it by appending a point reversed the winding and turned it inside out (97 of 119). Re-tracing the profile in the shell's direction fixed both, leaving 4 vertices on the recessed cap-face ring -- the same benign signature as the shell's base-plate rim. Separately, declaring the bung material textureless halved gpuBytesEstimate from 44.7 MB to 22.4 MB: the generator had been building a second full 1024-square canvas set for a 64 mm part. Known defect carried forward: the head plate renders with a radial pinwheel smear where the lathe's UVs converge at the cap centre, and reads blown out. That is a texture artefact and is material-pass's job.

reviewHistory.summary: Material-pass: the spec's localOverrides became pixels via a hand-written wear painter, because the generator passes them through as data and never reads them. Per-part colour delta-E fell 41.30 to 16.27 and Tier 1 passes at IoU 0.9152. Four defects were found and fixed, each by measurement rather than by eye. (1) The generator was loading referencePbr map FILES at runtime -- ten 404s and a black drum, because it had already forced colour to white and roughness to 1 on the strength of maps it believed it had; referencePbr is evidence, so the boundary adapter now resolves it to null and the procedural path is taken. (2) LatheGeometry's v is linear in profile INDEX, and this profile's body panels are one segment each, buying 3.9 m of drum per unit v against 0.21 m for a chime curl; placing oxide by v spilled it 144 mm up the lower panel, so all physical placement moved into metres through a v-to-height table. (3) The de-lit palette's darkest stop is luma 53 against a review backdrop of 58, so mottled enamel segmented as background and turntable_gate reported false interior holes on three of four azimuths; the enamel range was lifted to sit around the plate's own measured median of 67, with the missing specular range deliberately NOT baked into base colour. (4) The bung albedo was taken from the second palette stop rather than the first; direct measurement of the plate at the bung's location gave #605751, which both raised fidelity and cleared the per-part colour gate.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface-pass: no change, and the reason is structural rather than an omission. This pass owns normal/bump/AO locality, and all three already ship: the wear painter emits a normal map Sobel-derived from an INDEPENDENT height field (not from albedo, which is what the spec's normal.pattern promises) at strength 0.35, and an AO map that darkens the two hoop roots and both chime recesses in metres. They were authored in the material pass because they are computed from the same seeded height field as the oxide -- separating them would have meant generating that field twice and risking the two copies drifting. uv1 is aliased onto uv on the shell so aoMap is actually sampled rather than silently ignored, which a lathe's single UV set would otherwise cause. Gates re-run and hold: turntable clean on all four azimuths, Tier 1 IoU 0.9152, per-part colour delta-E 16.27.

reviewHistory.summary: Lighting-pass: the factory's own light rig is DELIBERATELY not what this prop ships with, and that is worth stating rather than leaving as a silent no-op. lightingFromPhoto records what was read off the plate -- a high key slightly camera-left, a soft fill, a strong hemisphere, no rim, ACES filmic at exposure 1.0, and explicitly NO contact shadow, because prepare-image.mjs rejects a plate that has one and the prop carries its own AO instead. But a thaikit prop is placed by a level builder into a scene that lights itself; the render harness supplies its own hemisphere, key, fill and rim and ignores the factory's. So this pass's output is the evidence record, not a shipped rig. One real consequence was measured and is recorded on the material: the harness has NO environment map, so a satin dielectric gets narrow highlights from three directional lights and the render's p95 luma reaches 71 against the plate's 105. That shortfall is left as a shortfall -- baking the missing specular range into base colour would have made the drum read wrong under every other lighting rig it will ever meet.

reviewHistory.summary: Interaction-pass: the runtime contract is deliberately minimal and matches the asset exactly -- ONE pivot (root, at base-center, +Y), ZERO sockets, ONE cylinder collider on the shell, ZERO destruction groups. That emptiness is a decision, not a gap: a sealed 200 litre drum has no moving parts and nothing attaches to it, so a named pivot or socket would be a promise the prop cannot keep. A previous attempt at this asset declared eight pivots and ten sockets for a welded steel cylinder, plus two revolute bung caps that do not unscrew. Measured off the built scene rather than read from the spec: pivots ['root'], sockets [], colliders ['drum-shell'], destructionGroups []. The boundary adapter derives destruction groups from the built nodes rather than assuming the list is empty, so a component that somehow carried a fractureGroup would fail promotion loudly instead of being dropped at the boundary; it also drops the empty collider records the generator writes for every component, because a nameless proxy in the runtime list reads as a physics shape that exists and does nothing. check_part_coverage passes with 2 named parts and 0 unnamed meshes, so the model is explodable and clickable. One nuance recorded rather than glossed: that gate excludes the componentTree ROOT, and here the drum shell is both the root and essentially all of the geometry, so only the bung was coverage-checked. The shell is the mesh every turntable, Tier 1 and silhouette measurement in this build is taken of.

reviewHistory.summary: Optimization-pass: nothing to optimise, because the budget was designed to in the blockout rather than optimised into at the end. Final measurement off the BUILT scene: 1864 triangles / 2000, 2 draw calls / 2, 2 materials / 2, 2 unique geometries / 2 -- at ceiling on three axes and 93 percent of the fourth. The two-component split IS the design, so there is nothing left to merge and no pivot hung off a part that would have had to be merged. No decimation: 44 radial segments at the 0.29 m hoop radius give 0.74 mm of chord error, 0.75 px on a 1024 px review render, so the tessellation tier was chosen up front and the authored profile points stay exact. VRAM is 22.4 MB across 4 canvas textures, halved from 44.7 MB by declaring the bung material textureless -- the generator had been building a second full 1024-square map set for a 64 mm part. Every gate re-run clean: turntable covered and unholed on all four azimuths, Tier 1 IoU 0.9152 / aspect 0.0027 / scale 0.0127 / per-part colour delta-E 16.27, attachment 0 unmeasured, part coverage 2 named parts and 0 unnamed. Honest shortfall recorded on rust-distribution: the plate carries more oxide and more contrast than the procedural field produces. Placement is right; amount is light.

notes.shell: 20 profile points x 44 radial segments x 2 = 1672.
notes.bung: 7 profile points x 16 radial segments x 2 = 192.
notes.chordError: 44 segments at the 0.29 m hoop radius is 0.74 mm, which is 0.75 px on a 1024 px render where the drum spans 590 px -- sub-pixel.
notes.capCost: Two of the 20 profile rings sit on the axis at r = 0.0001 and cost 176 near-degenerate triangles between them. That is what closes the shell into a SOLID; an open tube would show its own interior from above.
notes.headroom: 168 triangles are deliberately left unspent. render-model.mjs measures the built scene for real, and a spec authored exactly at its ceiling has no room to be 2 percent wrong.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The broad vertical specular band sits left of centre on each panel and the top chime crown is the brightest region in the plate, so the key is high and slightly to the camera-left.
The camera-right side of the drum never goes to black -- its darkest panel value is still well above the shadow floor -- which is a soft fill, not bounce.
The plate is a lightbox: prepare-image measured the backdrop at 243.6 mean luma with a 2.5 stdev, and there is no cast shadow anywhere in frame.
Deliberately absent. The plate has no rim separation -- the silhouette is defined by the backdrop being brighter than the object, not by a back light.
The plate is a lightbox with no clipped highlights outside the top chime crown, so exposure sits at 1.0 and ACES filmic keeps that crown from blowing out in the render the way a linear curve would.
lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: none -- there is no ground shadow in the plate and prepare-image.mjs rejects a contact shadow outright, because it bakes into the albedo as a permanent dark smear. The prop carries its own ambient occlusion instead: the AO response darkens the two hoop roots and both chime recesses, which is occlusion the geometry actually causes rather than a floor it is standing on.
lightingFromPhoto.groundShadow: left to the host scene; a level builder lights its own floor.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
